stem:
Meena's mother mixes wheat flour with yeast, sugar and warm water to make dough. After one hour the dough rises and becomes larger in size. She makes a second dough in the same way but without yeast, and it does not rise in the same way.
Why does the dough with yeast rise?

options.text: Yeast is a microorganism that grows in the warm dough and makes the dough rise after some time.
Warm water and flour rise on their own, so the yeast is not needed at all.
Yeast is only a flavouring powder and the sugar alone makes the dough rise.
The dough rises first, which then gives the yeast enough room to grow in it.

teacher.key_rationale: Yeast is a microorganism (fungus) that grows and acts in warm conditions; its activity in the dough causes the dough to rise after some time, while dough without yeast does not rise the same way. B drops the stated condition (yeast), C misattributes the rise to sugar and treats yeast as flavouring, and D reverses the cause-effect relationship.
